Legal
Privacy policy
How I handle the personal data you share with me through this website. Last updated: 20 October 2026.
Who I am

This website is run by Veselin Parashkevov, a freelance email marketer based in Bulgaria, working under the name FYRVEK. I am the controller of the personal data described here. You can reach me at hello@fyrvek.com.
What data I collect
Contact form: your name, email address, store URL, the service you select, and your message.
Email: anything you send to hello@fyrvek.com, including your email address and the content of your message.
Technical data: when you visit the site, the hosting provider automatically processes your IP address and basic browser information to deliver the pages and keep them secure.
I do not use analytics, advertising trackers or social media pixels, and this website does not set cookies.
Why I use it, and on what legal basis
To reply to your enquiry and prepare an offer at your request (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR, steps before entering into a contract).
To carry out the work if we agree on a project (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR, performance of a contract).
To keep the website secure and working (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, legitimate interest).
To keep records required by law, such as tax records (Article 6(1)(c) GDPR, legal obligation).
I do not add you to a mailing list, and I do not sell or rent your data to anyone.
Who processes the data for me
Web3Forms delivers contact form messages to my inbox.
Klaviyo stores your name, email address, store URL and the service you select, so I can send you an automatic confirmation of your request.
Google Workspace hosts my hello@fyrvek.com mailbox.
GitHub Pages hosts this website.

Some of these providers may process data outside the European Economic Area, including in the United States. Where that happens, the transfer relies on safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.
How long I keep it

Enquiries that do not lead to a project are deleted within 12 months. If we work together, I keep our correspondence and project records for as long as needed to complete the work, and longer only where the law requires it, for example for tax purposes.
Your rights
You can ask me to access, correct or delete your data, to restrict or object to its use, or to receive a copy of it. Write to hello@fyrvek.com and I will reply within one month.

You also have the right to complain to a data protection authority. In Bulgaria this is the Commission for Personal Data Protection (cpdp.bg). If you live elsewhere, you can contact the authority in your own country.
Changes
If this policy changes, I will update the date at the top of this page.

VESPERA: a full retention program for a candle brand
Post-purchase · Replenishment · Trio to full size · Win-back · Holiday campaigns · 13 emails
The brand
VESPERA makes hand-poured candles in stoneware vessels, sold as a small evening ritual: light it, put the phone down, stay a little longer at the table.
The problem

A candle is a slow product. It is bought once, often as a gift, and then the store goes quiet for months. By the time it burns down, the customer has forgotten where it came from, and the second order goes to whoever shows up first in their feed.
What I built
Thirteen emails that follow the candle, not the calendar.

Timed from delivery, not the order date. The care email (“The first burn sets the rest”) arrives three days after delivery, before the first long burn, and the review request two weeks later, when they have actually lived with it.
Two paths after checkout. First-time buyers get the ritual and the care guide. Repeat buyers skip it and see the collection instead.
A refill, not a resell. When about a quarter inch of wax is left, the email offers a $26 refill for the vessel they already love, against $38 for a new candle.
Win-back that leads with something new. A new seasonal scent first, a 15% code only in the second email, and a last email that asks one question: keep me on the list, or send fewer emails.
December planned backward from the Christmas shipping cutoff, so the last gift email still arrives in time.
What it’s built to do
Turn a one-time gift into an evening habit: one candle, then a refill, then a second scent, without discounting the brand into the ground.

SUNFOLD: abandoned cart, browse abandonment, launch and segmentation
Abandoned cart flow · Browse abandonment flow · Launch campaign · Segments · A/B tests · 7 emails
SUNFOLD is a skincare brand built for the summer feed: a shimmer body oil, a rice glow peel, two lip treatments and spot patches, all in bright peach and watermelon tones.

Skincare is easy to want and hard to buy online. People add a product, then stop to wonder if it will suit their skin, how long it lasts and what happens if they don’t like it. A generic “you forgot something” email answers none of that.

An abandoned cart flow that answers the doubt. Email 1, an hour later, simply shows the cart. Email 2 answers the three questions that stop a skincare purchase: how long a bottle lasts, whether it suits sensitive skin, and the 30-day promise with no need to send anything back.

A discount only where it changes the decision. The last email splits by cart value. Under $45, the shopper gets a 48-hour free-shipping code. Over $45, shipping is already free, so the email says so and keeps the margin.
Browse abandonment that knows what they looked at, with a dynamic block that swaps in the exact product, in five versions.
A launch with no discount at all. The limited Watermelon lip treatment goes to subscribers 24 hours early. The reward is being first, and “one batch, no restock” is true, so the urgency is real.
Segments and A/B tests for VIPs, repeat buyers and lapsed customers, so the next campaign goes to the right people.
Win back the carts that were one answer away from checkout, and protect the margin on the ones that would have bought anyway.

HALDEN Sport: welcome, replenishment and Black Friday emails
Welcome flow · Replenishment flow · BFCM campaign · 8 emails
HALDEN Sport sells three supplements, whey isolate, creatine and electrolytes, with one rule: every dose is printed on the front of the label. No proprietary blends.

Supplement shoppers have been burned before. They have bought tubs full of “blends” and promises, so a new brand starts with zero trust, and a protein tub that runs out quietly usually gets replaced by whatever is on sale that day.

A welcome flow that sells honesty, not hype. Email 1 gives the 15% code and asks the reader to turn their own tub around and look for the words “proprietary blend”. Email 2 argues for buying less: “You need fewer supplements than you think”, with one product for each goal.
A last-chance email that does the maths. Cost per serving for every product, so 15% off becomes something concrete, not just a number.

Replenishment timed to the scoop. At one scoop a day from the order date, the first email arrives with “about 7 scoops left”, early enough for the next tub to arrive before the last one runs out. The second email answers the subscription doubt: skip, change or cancel in two clicks.
Black Friday in three steps: early access for engaged subscribers, bundles picked by training goal, and a last day with a real deadline.
Compliance built in. Every claim stays inside supplement rules, with the required disclaimer in every footer.
Earn a sceptical buyer’s first order with transparency, then make the reorder so well timed that switching brands never comes up.
